description:
Goal

A demanded physical transport answer monotonically refines exact semantic producer/use relations into one ABI contract. ABI, backend, interpreter, and native consumers use that answer directly; no layer reselects identity from Ty, ShapeId, debug text, broad callsite summaries, or session inventories.

Signal

- The original enum-reduce fixture compiles warning-free with materially fewer products/events and no telemetry-only allocation.
- Every callsite-tagged callable return payload names only exact producer relations for its own surface.
- One producer used by several invocation endpoints and one endpoint reached by several producers settle one common physical return contract.
- Boundary wrappers emit that contract; caller continuations adapt it to caller-local ExecutableReturn or untagged resume layouts.
- Forward/reverse service, equal reproduction, replacement, withdrawal, and unrelated-reader coldness agree.
- Full library tests, strict all-target clippy, formatting, targeted interpreter/JIT fixtures, and release telemetry/performance gates pass.

North-star constraints

- One requested product reads exact current fact/product authorities or returns exact waits. There is no seal, pass, whole-world census, session scan, no-change signal, or downstream reconstruction.
- Only actual product back-edges form a local settlement group, and only settled immutable answers publish.
- Physical ids are values, never semantic owners. Exact TransportPosition owners and semantic flow relations survive until physical interning.
- A fix must remove obsolete selectors, inventories, duplicated authorities, and stale representation tests rather than preserve them.
- Telemetry emitters pass borrowed raw authorities and minimal scalars; handlers alone inspect, transform, or retain.

Established foundation

fz-k22.5.1 supplies immutable revisioned products, exact durable fact/product dependencies, final movement states, replaceable per-publisher contributions, exact incoming-input relations, and targeted retraction.

The spike has proved the intended lower model for ordinary positions: ExecutableInput owns its ABI from settled ActivationInputs plus RuntimeDemand; CallArg conforms to the selected input; ExecutableFacts owns normalized local structure without copied Ty/demand/layout data; TransportShape and CallableConstruction are separate position-owned product domains; exact recursive TransportShape and pass-through CallableConstruction back-edges settle atomically; callable/boundary facts embed through ABI/backend values instead of physical-id inventories. The legacy closure/component solver, demanded-id stores, global callable/boundary products, selector/fallback paths, and custom freshness ledgers are deletion targets.

Newly proven return-source fault

The earlier hypothesis that callable target return demand was missing is false. In both discordant enum-predicate traces, every caller endpoint has the exact same interned Ty and TupleFields([Whole, Whole]) demand as the selected target, and the target already carries that demand. boundary_return_demands = Vec::new() is obsolete scaffolding, not the cause.

The first wrong fact is the source recipe. Callsite-tagged ReturnPayload and ResumePayload are callee/boundary source ABIs, while ExecutableReturn and untagged ResumePayload are caller-local destinations. Current transport conflates them: it gives a source payload caller-local type/demand authority and reconstructs producer anchors from TransportSource::CallsiteReturn over the broad CallSiteSummary.

Concrete proof:
- F203/Ty139 surface [Ty30,Ty38] has one exact F174/Ty140 relation; the summary happens to match, so the endpoint matches the target.
- Sibling F203/Ty150 has exact F174, three F175 activations, and F178 for that surface, but the summary walks seven targets including other surfaces [Ty21,Ty38] and [Ty112,Ty38]. Cross-surface reconstruction changes the endpoint layout.
- F203/Ty275 surface [Ty21,Ty84] has exact F176+F177 producers, all Shape23, yet its summary-derived endpoint is Shape20. Its sibling exact set is only F177 and correctly remains Shape23.
- Exact producer sets are not always physically concordant: F203/Ty150 receives Shape17 from F174/F175 and Shape13 from F178; its legitimate common endpoint contract is Shape20. Replacing the summary with one selected target is therefore also wrong.

Required model proof before implementation

The semantic graph is bipartite: a callable producer/surface boundary return connects to every exact CallableInvocationReturn endpoint it can serve; an endpoint connects to every exact producer/surface that can reach it. Target ExecutableReturn layouts are anchors. Every connected ABI node must settle one common representation because an indirect call has one static continuation signature and a boxed callable has one wrapper signature for that surface.

Prove this with:
1. the two real discordances;
2. one producer reaching two endpoints;
3. one endpoint reached by structurally different producer returns;
4. a connected P-A/P-B/Q-B graph;
5. the existing enum-take three-lane producer/two-lane caller case, showing the common source contract and the caller continuation adapter at the correct boundary;
6. generic/opaque and uncalled publication cases.

The candidate is an exact semantic callable-return-source relation carried upstream with RuntimeDemand contributions. Transport converts those identities into producer/surface boundary-return and callsite-payload product edges. Genuine back-edges settle only their exact TransportShape SCC. This candidate is acceptable only if the spikes prove finite monotone equations, exact dependency/retraction behavior, schedule independence, and no copied demand/Ty/provenance snapshot.

Implementation strategy after proof

1. Pin production-path intent tests for exact source membership and common ABI settlement; classify old tests as semantic invariants, obsolete representation pins, or resource ceilings.
2. Preserve exact producer/surface-to-invocation relations in the semantic demand model. Do not query a reverse index or rescan a session.
3. Give source payloads and semantic boundary returns explicit position ownership, settle only real return-contract back-edges, and make boundary construction consume that answer. Caller-local destination layouts remain independent and are adapted by the existing continuation path.
4. Collapse obsolete CallableReturnAuthority selection, broad CallsiteReturn source reconstruction, empty boundary-return-demand scaffolding, and any wrapper-side compensation made unnecessary by the corrected ownership direction.
5. Finish the wider position-owned cutover, embed owner values in artifacts, delete legacy inventories/solvers/tests, update northstar and agent docs, remove every spike/probe, then run all gates and telemetry/performance comparisons.

fz-k22.30 remains blocked until this lands. fz-k22.31 owns only the genuinely uncalled first-class discrepancy if it remains after the common-contract model is proven.
title: Make transport shape a product-owned refinement
